headline: High: Superset can egress data while the paired prompt-leakage agent has no shared-channel protections, creating default leakage and injection risks if outputs are bridged.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: No direct shared channel is documented, but Superset can call APIs and has allowlisted egress, while system_prompts_leaks is explicitly about prompt leakage. If Superset outputs are copied into the other agent or a shared workspace exists, attacker-controlled content could be treated as instructions. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF the two agents exchange text through copy-paste, files, or a shared queue
IF Superset renders untrusted content that the other agent parses as instructions
mitigations: Disable any manual copy-paste bridge between outputs
Keep the agents in separate workspaces
Add a provenance label to all imported text
Require a human review step before reusing outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the bridge

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both profiles show no data classes touched and no shared filesystem or OAuth principal is documented. Superset has allowlisted egress, but system_prompts_leaks has network egress none, so the pairwise leakage path is not evidenced beyond general docs-only inference. That supports low rather than medium.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same sensitive workspace
IF Superset is configured to ingest files containing secrets
mitigations: Keep sensitive files out of any shared directory
Run each agent under a separate OS account
Verify no shared OAuth tokens are mounted
Restrict Superset to non-sensitive datasets
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Superset exposes API calls and allowlisted egress, while system_prompts_leaks has no write or network capabilities documented. There is no evidence of overlapping mutable resources, locking issues, or shared write surfaces, so a capability conflict is only plausible under unusual orchestration, not in default settings.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable backend
IF an orchestrator grants them shared write access not shown in the profiles
mitigations: Avoid sharing the same database or git repo
Use separate credentials per agent
Disable concurrent writes to shared resources
Check the orchestrator for implicit locking
requires-engineering: add resource-level locks

D_cascading_error.rationale: Superset can produce API-driven analytics outputs, and system_prompts_leaks is a prompt-leakage-oriented agent that may consume text without documented verification. If Superset output is fed into the second agent as authoritative input, errors or fabricated claims can cascade into downstream leakage or actions. The interaction is inferred, so uncertainty favors medium.
conditions: IF Superset output is reused as input to the other agent
IF the second agent lacks an explicit verification step
mitigations: Insert a human verification step
Require source citations before reuse
Mark upstream outputs as untrusted
Limit downstream actions to read-only summaries
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent, and both profiles show empty data_classes_touched. Without a documented compliance mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF either agent is later assigned regulated data such as PHI or EU PII
mitigations: Do not route regulated data to either agent
Document data residency requirements before deployment
Review retention settings if sensitive data is introduced
